Q: Apache mod rewrite - www for all except one A:

Exclude app-ads.txt explicitly in the RewriteCond, not as a separate RewriteRule.

✅ Working .htaccess

Options +FollowSymLinks
RewriteEngine On

# Exclude app-ads.txt from redirect
RewriteCond %{REQUEST_URI} !^/app-ads\.txt$ [NC]
RewriteCond %{HTTP_HOST} !^www\.example\.com$ [NC]
RewriteRule ^(.*)$ https://www.example.com/$1 [R=301,L]

# ... more rules

📌 Why your attempt failed

You tried:

RewriteRule ^app-ads\.txt$ - [L]

This does not work because:

  • Rewrite rules are processed top-down

  • Your redirect rule already fired before this exception

  • Once a redirect happens, processing stops

So the exception must be inside the redirect logic itself.

📂 Where to place app-ads.txt

Place the file physically at:

/public_html/app-ads.txt

(or your document root)

Google will then successfully access:

https://example.com/app-ads.txt

❌ It will not be redirected
✅ Google AdMob verification will pass

🔍 How to test

Run in terminal:

curl -I https://example.com/app-ads.txt

Expected result:

HTTP/2 200

NOT:

301 Moved Permanently

✅ Google requirement (clarification)

Google requires:

https://example.com/app-ads.txt

Redirecting it (even to www) invalidates the file.

Q: What is the system call interface? A:

The C function is just a "wrapper" or a middleman. It makes it easier for you to use the System Call Interface without needing to know the complex internal hardware details

for example

  1. The C function open() is a "Wrapper" function in User Mode that acts as a user-friendly API for the programmer.

  2. It does not perform the task itself; instead, it puts a System Call ID into a CPU register.

  3. The System Call Interface is the boundary that intercepts this ID and triggers a switch from User Mode to Kernel Mode.

  4. The Interface uses a System Call Table to find the actual OS code (the implementation) corresponding to that ID.

  5. In short: The C function is the request, the Interface is the bridge, and the Kernel code is the execution.

Q: "Undefined function g" when role created via enforcer's API A:

It's a bug, and the auther just fixed it, you can fix it by upgrading casbin to v3.8.1 or higher.

It's v3, not v2 any more, v2 seems not fixed.

And, if you're using gorm-adapter, make sure upgrade to newest version, which is also upgraded to use casbin v3, instead of v2.

If any tool still using v2, then you may raise an issue on github to request upgrade it to use casbin v3, so that get the latest bug fix.
